deck_metadata.title: Offer management is a system problem
deck_metadata.purpose: Benchmark Gera, VTEX, Yalo, TudoFarma, and BEES Offer Creator
deck_metadata.subtitle: What posture should BEES take toward promotion orchestration?
deck_metadata.source: [Research] [One] Gera and Offer Creating Tools Benchmark | Q2 2026
deck_metadata.executive_summary: The benchmark shifts the question from improving Offer Creator usability to deciding how BEES should participate in a broader promotion-orchestration ecosystem.
key_implications: Gera combines promotion calendars, portfolio management, BI, distributor acceptance, and sales-force incentives.
BEES Offer Creator is a channel-native execution tool, but it does not replace a central orchestration layer.
VTEX and TudoFarma demonstrate faster or simpler native creation; Yalo demonstrates the value of a front-end conversational layer.
The strategic decision is whether BEES should integrate, compete, or explore a corporate transaction.

slides.title: Offer management is a system problem, not only a tool problem
slides.takeaway: Promotions connect manufacturer strategy, distributor execution, sales-rep incentives, channel visibility, and ROI.
evidence: Gera combines promotion calendars, portfolio management, sales-force incentives, and BI.
BEES Offer Creator creates offers inside the BEES ecosystem but does not replace every upstream ERP or orchestration need.
Strategic partners may operate BEES, Gera, VTEX, Yalo, and ERP tools simultaneously.
slides.recommendation: Decide BEES posture at ecosystem level before expanding Offer Creator feature scope.

slides.title: Gera is the only benchmarked player positioned as a full indirect-channel orchestrator
slides.takeaway: The differentiation is not offer creation alone; it is coordination across actors and systems.
evidence: Gera: calendar, portfolio, BI, distributor workflow, sales-force incentives.
VTEX: native commerce promotions and integrations, but not indirect-channel specific.
Yalo: conversational front end; upstream systems provide promotion logic.
slides.recommendation: Treat Gera as a strategic ecosystem signal, not only as a feature benchmark.
slides.source: Research page 6198329781 · Summary of Findings

slides.title: BEES Offer Creator is useful where the channel is the execution surface
slides.takeaway: The native tool remains relevant, but its boundaries become visible when partners run multiple systems.
evidence: Five Brazilian partners are reported as current Offer Creator users.
Partners with existing promotion integrations may not need a separate native creator.
ERP price guardrails can cancel orders when BEES promotions are not reflected upstream.
slides.recommendation: Preserve native execution while defining a clear integration contract with upstream promotion owners.
slides.source: Research page 6198329781 · About Offer Creator

signals.label: Plan

signals.label: Govern
signals.detail: Distributors can accept or reject campaigns before execution.

signals.detail: Rules, quotas, and incentives reach sales-force workflows.

slides.title: The alternatives solve different parts of the problem
slides.takeaway: No competitor is a complete substitute for BEES; each reveals a different product opportunity.
evidence: VTEX: faster single-screen creation, recurrence, and mature commerce integrations.
Yalo: conversational front end and recommendations, but no native promotion engine.
TudoFarma: fast bulk creation, distributor/state toggles, and simple pharma-specific UX.
slides.recommendation: Borrow patterns by job: orchestration from Gera, native speed from VTEX, reach from Yalo, and simplicity from TudoFarma.
slides.source: Research page 6198329781 · VTEX, Yalo, and TudoFarma findings

composition_spec.reading_mode: Fast judgment: large marks, explicit ranking, one dominant contrast, minimal annotation.

slides.title: The strategic choice is integration, competition, or acquisition
slides.takeaway: Each posture changes the time-to-value, control, and partner migration burden.

hypotheses.evidence: Preserves partner investment but introduces dependency and semantic gaps.
Could unify the stack but requires long delivery and broad domain scope.
Could absorb capabilities and relationships; feasibility and fit are unvalidated.

slides.recommendation: Run a time-boxed integration discovery before committing to build or M&A.
slides.source: Research page 6198329781 · Conclusion and strategic considerations

slides.title: Start with an integration posture, guarded by evidence
slides.takeaway: The first decision should preserve partner momentum while testing whether Gera’s orchestration model fits BEES execution.
slides.recommendation: Define an API and operating-model discovery with Colgate or another shared partner.

guardrails.label: Keep
guardrails.body: BEES visibility before checkout and native marketplace execution.

guardrails.label: Change
guardrails.body: Offer lifecycle, upstream acknowledgement, budget status, and partner workflow.

guardrails.label: Watch
guardrails.body: Eligibility semantics, real-time sync, distributor adoption, and switching cost.
